verticalInfoCards.title: Rituals and Aarti
verticalInfoCards.note: Pilgrims can take a holy dip in the Tapt Kund (natural hot spring) before entering the temple. Special pujas can be booked online.

quote.text: “At Badrinath, the serene chants and the warmth of the Tapt Kund wash away sins, leaving the heart pure and devoted to Lord Vishnu.”
quote.author: — A Pilgrim's Reflection

verticalInfoCards.description: The temple rituals are performed by priests from the Nambudiri Brahmin community. The atmosphere is filled with devotion, highlighted by the continuous recitation of Vedic hymns and scriptures.

overview.title: Overview
overview.text: Badrinath Temple, located on the banks of the Alaknanda River, is a sacred Hindu shrine dedicated to Lord Vishnu. It is one of the four key sites in the Char Dham pilgrimage and is revered as one of the 108 Divya Desams, holy shrines for Vaishnavites.

mythology.title: Mythological Origin
mythology.text: According to legend, Lord Vishnu sought a serene place for meditation. He found this spot, but it was exposed to harsh weather. To protect him, his consort Goddess Lakshmi took the form of a giant Badri (jujube) tree, sheltering him. Pleased by her devotion, Vishnu named the place Badrika Ashram, and he is worshipped here as Badrinath, the lord of the Badri forest.

architecture.title: Architectural Highlights
points: Features a brightly painted facade with a tall arched gateway, a classic example of Garhwali wooden architecture.
Located on the banks of the Alaknanda River, with the Tapt Kund, a natural hot water spring, situated just below.
The main sanctum (Garbhagriha) houses a 1-meter tall black stone (saligram) image of Lord Badrinarayan.
The temple has a conical roof, about 15 meters tall, topped with a small cupola and a golden gilt.
The current structure was established by Adi Shankaracharya in the 8th century.

significance.title: Spiritual Significance
points: The foremost of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites, considered essential for attaining salvation (moksha).
One of the 108 Divya Desams, the holy abodes of Lord Vishnu.
The area is also known as 'Bhooloka Vaikuntha,' meaning 'Vaikuntha (heavenly abode of Vishnu) on Earth'.
The deity is believed to be in a meditative posture, signifying peace and spiritual welfare for all humanity.
During winter, the idol is moved to the Narsimha Temple in Joshimath for worship.

events.event: Mentioned in Vedic scriptures and Puranas like the Bhagavata Purana.
Re-established as a major pilgrimage site by Adi Shankaracharya.
Renovated and expanded by the Kings of Garhwal.
Became highly accessible with modern road construction.
A primary pilgrimage destination attracting millions of devotees annually.

items.text: Bathing in the Tapt Kund is believed to have medicinal and spiritual healing properties, cleansing one's sins.
The nearby Charanpaduka rock is believed to bear the footprints of Lord Vishnu.
It is believed that the sages Nara and Narayana, dual incarnations of Vishnu, still meditate in the surrounding mountains.
In winter, the chief priest (Rawal) relocates to Joshimath to continue the worship of the deity.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Badrinath is more than a temple; it is a symbol of unwavering faith and spiritual solace. A pilgrimage to this divine abode offers a profound experience of peace, devotion, and a deep connection with Lord Vishnu in his most serene form.

aboutPostCards.title: Major Festivals
items: Mata Murti Ka Mela – Celebrates the descent of the river Ganga.
Badri Kedar Utsav – A cultural and religious festival celebrated in both Badrinath and Kedarnath.
Krishna Janmashtami – Lord Krishna's birthday is celebrated with special pujas.
Temple Opening & Closing Ceremonies – Grand ceremonies mark the opening (April/May) and closing (Oct/Nov) of the temple.

aboutPostCards.title: Nearby Attractions
items: Mana Village – The last Indian village before the Tibet/China border.
Tapt Kund & Narad Kund – Natural hot and cold water springs.
Neelkanth Peak – A majestic snow-covered peak forming a stunning backdrop.
Vasudhara Falls – A scenic waterfall requiring a short trek from Mana.
Charanpaduka – A rock believed to have the footprints of Lord Vishnu.

methods.title: By Road
methods.description: Badrinath is well-connected by motorable roads. Buses and taxis are available from major Uttarakhand towns like Rishikesh and Haridwar.

methods.title: By Helicopter
methods.description: Helicopter services are available from Dehradun and Phata to Badrinath, especially during the pilgrimage season.

methods.title: Nearest Airport
methods.description: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (approx. 314 km away).

mapSection.title: Temple Location
mapSection.description: At 3,133m in Uttarakhand’s Chamoli district, situated between the Nar and Narayana mountain ranges.
